editorial:
Imagine meeting the love of your life after both of you have already died. That is the wild setup here. You follow Kenjo and Haruka, two people who suffered terrible ends in the 90s during some really dark times in Tokyo. Kenjo was taken out by a gas attack, and Haruka had a much more violent end on the streets. The movie jumps forward to 2002, where these two souls find each other again. It feels like a dream and a nightmare at the same time, mixing a sad mood with a strange sense of hope. You will feel the weight of their loss, but the way they reconnect keeps you interested in where their story is going.

What really works is the acting, as you can feel the raw pain and love between the leads. The pacing is a bit slow, which might bug some of you, but it helps you sink into the mood. If you like stories about fate and the afterlife, you will love this. You should definitely try to find a high-quality 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection so you can see all the gritty detail of the city. If you are just browsing, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to experience it without spending too much.
endingExplained: At the end, Kenjo and Haruka realize that their connection is stronger than death itself. They stop fighting the pain of how they died and choose to embrace each other in a spiritual way. The twist is that their reunion allows them to finally find peace and move on together. They stop being ghosts of their past mistakes and vanish into a light, showing that love can fix even the worst tragedies.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves tragic romance and stories about the afterlife.
